Selected projects

Historical simulation and digital media: two projects, their context, and the systems behind them.

I.

Steam and Steel

Game modification / Medieval II: Total War

A total-conversion modification for Medieval II: Total War: Kingdoms, set in the late Victorian era. The project brings a world-spanning historical setting into an existing strategy-game framework.

This entry brings together the project’s public release information and provides a place for future development notes on historical interpretation, game systems, and implementation.

Project context

Historical setting

The late nineteenth century provides the setting for a global campaign. The public project description emphasises research and the communication of this period’s history.

Development notes

Future notes here can document individual design decisions, the sources that informed them, and the practical limits of implementing them in Medieval II.

II.

newsletter-media.com

Media start-up / Meerkat

A media start-up supported by Meerkat, a news aggregation and publishing system. The architecture separates the work of collecting and processing news from the service that delivers articles to readers.

The supplied Meerkat diagram describes a scheduled pipeline on AWS: ingesting articles, translating and analysing them, and publishing results to PostgreSQL. A Flask API serves applications and web readers; cover images are delivered separately.

Visit newsletter-media.comDownload original diagram

Architecture notes

Collection and analysis

EventBridge schedules a Fargate task every two hours. The diagram identifies news publishers as input sources, DeepSeek for translation and analysis, and DeepL as a translation fallback.

Publication and delivery

Processing state and reader-facing data use separate PostgreSQL schemas. A publication transaction updates the serving data. The Flask service handles API requests, shared links and article pages, while S3 and CloudFront provide image storage and delivery.

Supporting services

The diagram also documents verification email through SES, subscription events through RevenueCat, and operational services for logs, container images and secret management.

This overview describes the supplied design document; it is not a live infrastructure status report.
